title: The Borrowed Parish
premise: Retired detective Oscar Dunmore has spent a decade hiding in a failing bookshop in the coastal village of Marrow Bay, quietly solving three deaths the police dismissed as accidents. When a missing woman's diary arrives at his shop—entries continuing weeks past her disappearance—he realizes she may still be alive, or someone wants the village to believe she is. His investigation unravels the parish's cherished history, implicating the beloved vicar who once saved Oscar from ruin. In the end, Oscar exposes the vicar's daughter as the woman who staged her own death to escape him, forcing Oscar to choose between the loyalty he owes and the truth he cannot bury—and he chooses truth, at the cost of his last refuge in the village.
about_author: Edmund Coldharbour is the pen name of a former parish clerk who spent thirty years recording the small cruelties of English village life. He writes from a house overlooking a churchyard, where he claims the best plots arrive by funeral procession.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sells Endings
chapters.summary: Oscar Dunmore's POV. A quiet morning in his failing bookshop establishes his routines, his anonymity, and the three unsanctioned cases that haunt his retirement. Emotional beat: weary contentment masking loneliness, as he catalogs books no one buys and memories no one shares.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A parcel arrives containing Marion Ellery's diary—missing for six weeks—its final entries dated nine days after her disappearance. The handwriting is unmistakably hers. Emotional beat: cold shock; the safe life Oscar built cracks open as he realizes the case everyone closed is breathing.

chapters.title: What the Constable Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Oscar visits PC Halloway under the pretense of donating books. Halloway's evasiveness about the Ellery search reveals pressure from above. Emotional beat: simmering frustration; Oscar recognizes the smell of a case steered shut.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Kindness
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with flashback. Reverend Aldous Crane—who once gave Oscar shelter after his disgrace—urges the village to stop speculating about Marion. Oscar feels gratitude warring with suspicion. Emotional beat: the ache of doubting the one man who never abandoned him.

chapters.title: A Diary That Lies by Telling Truth
chapters.summary: Oscar studies the diary's late entries, noting details only Marion would know—and one she couldn't: a description of his own shop's interior. Someone is writing to him specifically. Emotional beat: creeping dread turning into grim excitement; the detective in him wakes.

chapters.title: Marion's Sister, Marion's Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews Beth Ellery, who insists her sister would never vanish voluntarily, yet flinches at mention of the church. Emotional beat: grief laced with a guarded secret; Oscar leaves knowing Beth is protecting someone—perhaps herself.

chapters.title: The Third Case, Reopened
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He reviews his three quiet resolutions and realizes all three deaths touched the parish council, the body Crane's daughter Vivian chairs. Emotional beat: vertigo; the pattern he once dismissed as coincidence now forms a corridor pointing toward the family that saved him.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Timetables
chapters.summary: Oscar reconstructs Marion's last known day: a bus ticket never used, boots dry despite claimed coastal walks. She never left Marrow Bay by land or sea. Emotional beat: methodical calm over rising alarm—someone with local knowledge erased her.

chapters.title: An Anonymous Warning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A note in his letterbox: 'The parish keeps its own records. Stop reading them.' That night his shop window is shattered, nothing stolen. Emotional beat: violation and defiance; invisibility, he realizes, was always borrowed, never owned.

chapters.title: Vivian Crane's Perfect Alibi
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews Vivian, polished and pitying, who produces witnesses for every hour of Marion's disappearance. Too perfect. Emotional beat: admiration curdling into certainty; Oscar recognizes an alibi built by someone who learned detection from watching him.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Following a diary clue, Oscar searches the church undercroft and finds Marion's coat, a burner phone, and a list of parish council payments. Emotional beat: triumphant discovery shadowed by horror—the trail leads into the vicarage itself.

chapters.title: Confession Over Tea
chapters.summary: Crane invites Oscar for tea and, gently, asks him to let Marion rest. He knows what Oscar found. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the vicar's plea is love and threat in the same voice, and Oscar understands his refuge was always conditional.

chapters.title: Beth Breaks
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Confronted with the coat, Beth admits she helped Marion disappear—from Vivian, who was blackmailing her. Emotional beat: pity and anger entangled; the missing woman wanted to be missing.

chapters.title: The Blackmail Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar decodes the payments: Vivian has been extorting half the parish council for years, and Marion, the council's treasurer, found the ledger. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the motive was never money but exposure; Marion was going to confess everything.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Ink
chapters.summary: Oscar realizes the post-disappearance diary entries are Vivian's forgery, meant to convince the village Marion fled abroad—until entries began describing his shop, a taunt or a lure. Emotional beat: the hunter feels the hook; he has been summoned, not warned.

chapters.title: Halloway's Debt
chapters.summary: Oscar leverages PC Halloway, revealing the constable buried a report years ago to protect Crane. Halloway agrees to help—quietly. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; loyalty and truth begin pulling in opposite directions for everyone in the parish.

chapters.title: Where the Lighthouse Doesn't Reach
chapters.summary: Following the burner's last signal, Oscar finds a derelict chapel on the headland and signs of recent habitation. Marion may be alive, hiding from both Vivian and the law. Emotional beat: desperate hope; for the first time the case could end in rescue rather than another quiet burial.

chapters.title: The Trap at Evensong
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vivian, aware he's closing in, uses Crane to summon Oscar to the church, intending to frame him for Marion's murder and the shop fire that follows. Emotional beat: betrayal at its sharpest—the vicarage weaponizes the very loyalty it once gave him.

chapters.title: Ash on the Psalms
chapters.summary: The bookshop burns. Oscar, warned by Beth, escapes with the diary and ledger, and the village finally sees Vivian's hand in the flames. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve; his borrowed invisibility is ash, and he stops mourning it.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Oscar and Halloway reach Marion before Vivian's hired man does. She surrenders the original ledger and testifies. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; the dead woman is alive, and the living lie begins to die.

chapters.title: Vivian's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Confronted in the vestry, Vivian confesses with terrifying composure; Crane, shattered, refuses to shield her. Arrest at the church door. Emotional beat: grim catharsis—truth wins, but it arrives wearing the face of everything Oscar loved.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Parish
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Oscar rebuilds the shop with village help, no longer invisible but no longer hiding. He keeps one shelf for Marion's testimony and one empty for whatever comes next. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging; Oscar learns a parish can only be borrowed—truth must be owned.
